title: Toolbar actions
description: Topbar action group rendering left/right anchor buttons. Bridges legacy command/app shapes via COMMAND_HREFS.

documentation.purpose: Toolbar layout: two horizontal IconButton clusters separated by a `flex: 1` spacer. Renders nothing if both `left` + `right` arrays are empty. Each action is either `{ href, icon, label, external? }` (link) or `{ command, icon, label }` (built-in command resolved via `COMMAND_HREFS` map). IconButton uses `render={<a href>}` so middle-click + right-click → Copy link work natively.

reads.purpose: Action descriptors — declared inline in admin.json and passed as React props by mountApp.

states.renders: Row layout — left cluster + spacer + right cluster.

interactions.effect: Native anchor navigation. External actions open in new tab.
Native browser behavior — opens in new tab. Works because IconButton renders as `<a>`.

a11y.screen-reader: IconButton's `label` prop doubles as the assistive-tech label and the tooltip.

constraints.note: `COMMAND_HREFS` translates legacy `command` ids (`core/new-post`, `core/new-page`) to hash URLs. Adding more requires updating the table.
Render-prop swap is required: `<IconButton render={<a href target rel/>}/>`. The plain `href` prop is dropped by Base UI Button.
All actions resolve to URLs. There's no `onClick`-only callback action — keep dispatching to `core:command-palette` or a separate app for command-style invocations.

WP-admin's unlayered `a { color: var(--wp-admin-theme-color) }` wins against `@wordpress/ui` IconButton's layered color. The bundled `core:default` engine ships `.wp-admin-shell-region--toolbar a { color: var(--wpds-color-fg-interactive-neutral) }` (+ `:hover/:focus/:active` variants). A non-WPDS engine MUST emit an equivalent unlayered rule for its toolbar scheme.
`@wordpress/icons` SVGs lack `fill`. The bundled `core:default` engine forces `.wp-admin-shell-region--toolbar svg { fill: currentColor }`. A non-WPDS engine MUST do the same.
